_doc: WHERE WE LOOK, AND WHY THE TIER MATTERS MORE THAN THE LIST.
Indian ticketing is stratified, and the stratification is the whole signal. Self-serve
platforms (tier 'longtail') will list anybody who uploads an event, so that is where an
artist first appears. Curated platforms (tier 'major') are gatekept — a promoter or the
platform itself decides you are worth a slot. An artist moving from longtail to major is
the single loudest early-phase event this tool can observe, because somebody with money
changed their mind about them. That transition is PLATFORM GRADUATION and signals.py
scores it heavily.
BOOKMYSHOW AND DISTRICT ARE PRIMARY VALIDATION SOURCES. A long-tail or self-serve
listing only discovers an entity; it never confirms a major-platform booking.
BookMyShow is bounded to 12 category grids and 36 depth-one event-detail pages. Its
10-item grid teaser is never evidence. The strategy is fixture-tested, not token-live
validated as of 2026-08-21. District is direct plain HTTP: nine bounded routes use
Next.js EventData plus /events JSON-LD, with route category retained where observed.
Every active source states its source_role. Townscript is discovery-only and postponed.
Verification dates are per source. Re-run source health after a site change; record
what was observed rather than what was assumed.
'categories' is not decoration. The platform's own category label is the PRIMARY genre
signal in genres.classify_genre(), because a large share of clean listings carry no genre
word in the title at all ('Kanan Gill: Yes I'm Fine'). The crawler must capture it.

sources.name: BookMyShow
sources.notes: PRIMARY VALIDATION. The grid JSON-LD remains a 10-item teaser and is never accepted as evidence. As of 2026-08-21 the supported route is a bounded Apify browser-plus-residential-proxy crawl: render 12 category grids, follow only up to 36 depth-one event-detail URLs, then parse standard Event JSON-LD. Static fixtures prove more than 10 detail records; no token-backed live full-grid run is verified. If unconfigured, report it and retain prior raw data.

yield_measured.note: JSON-LD is capped at numberOfItems:10 and roughly two thirds of those are stale or venue entries. Measured across 3 pages: 30 events, 9 upcoming. comedy-shows-bengaluru returned ZERO upcoming.

sources.name: District (Zomato)
sources.notes: PRIMARY VALIDATION. Direct plain HTTP exposes 12 Event JSON-LD rows at /events and 12 structured Next.js EventData records on /activities/comedy-shows-in-bengaluru (both observed 2026-08-21); a detail Event JSON-LD was also confirmed. Fetch only the nine listed bounded routes. Route category is recorded; false is_available remains unknown, never Sold Out.

sources.name: Insider.in (legacy)
sources.notes: DISABLED. 502 Bad Gateway on every path (probe 2026-08-19). Superseded by District after the Paytm Insider migration. Kept in this file so old snapshots stay resolvable; re-enable only if it starts answering again.

sources.name: Skillbox
sources.notes: All three paths return 200 to a plain request but publish NO JSON-LD, so the listings must be parsed out of HTML — that is Apify work, not urllib work.

sources.name: Townscript
sources.notes: POSTPONED as of 2026-08-21. This self-serve long-tail channel remains discovery-only and is disabled until a maintainable HTML adapter is separately approved and fixture-tested.

sources.name: AllEvents
sources.notes: BEST SOURCE SO FAR. Plain HTTP + JSON-LD, 15-64 structured events per page, venue and date on 100% of rows. TWO TRAPS. (1) Some cities ignore the category segment and serve the same list for every path — measured Mumbai 0% comedy/music overlap (real filtering) vs Bengaluru 92% (none). fetch_listings.py detects this per city and drops the labels. (2) PUNE IS UNREACHABLE: /pune 404s and /pune-city 302s to /pine-city, a different place entirely. Excluded until a working slug is found.

sources.name: MeraEvents
sources.notes: /india-events now 404s; only the homepage answers, with no JSON-LD. Lowest priority.

sources.name: HighApe
sources.notes: Plain HTTP + JSON-LD, 265 structured events on the homepage alone. NO category field, so genre comes from the title or stays unknown. Metro nightlife bias.

discovery_queries._doc: SERP fallbacks for when a listing crawl is blocked, and the mechanism that finds platforms NOT in this file. Any ticketing domain appearing in these results that is not registered above is reported as a candidate NEW CHANNEL — that is the 'new channels of entertainment' half of the brief, and it is genre-agnostic on purpose: the next format nobody has named yet will surface here first.

_access_legend.direct-jsonld: Plain HTTP + schema.org JSON-LD. tools/fetch_listings.py handles these in Python — free, fast, structured, no Apify and no LLM in the loop.
_access_legend.direct-nextjs-eventdata: Plain HTTP Next.js Flight EventData plus /events JSON-LD. Route categories are retained; unknown availability is never scored as Sold Out.
_access_legend.apify-html: Answers a plain request but publishes no JSON-LD; listings need parsing out of HTML. Claude fetches these with Apify.
_access_legend.apify-browser-proxy: Refuses plain requests. Needs browser rendering behind a residential proxy. Currently only BookMyShow.
_access_legend.dead: Not answering. Disabled; left here so historical snapshots resolve.

_probe.note: Re-run after any source change. It records what was OBSERVED, and those observations belong in this file rather than in anyone memory.
